This runbook is the operational document for humans and AI monitoring agents:
how to run builds, what healthy output looks like, and how to interpret
failures and skips.

## Project facts (auto-generated)

- **Project:** `zeeker-judgements`
- **Database file:** `zeeker-judgements.db` (Datasette database name: `zeeker-judgements`)
- **Title:** Singapore Court Judgments
- **Description:** Non-commercial catalogue of Singapore court judgments from the Singapore Courts' free judgments portal on eLitigation (https://www.elitigation.sg/gd/): case metadata and AI-generated research summaries, with a link back to each judgment. Covers SGCA, SGHC, SGHCA, SGHCF, SGHCR, SGDC, SGFC, SGMC, and tribunals such as SGCDT and SGSCT — the crawler accepts any SG* court code that appears on the portal's listing — back to 2000. Full judgment text is collected for indexing and summarisation, but access to it is not provided through this catalogue — read each judgment at its source_url, where the PDF copy is the authoritative version (eLitigation warns its web-converted HTML 'may have created formatting or alignment issues'). Judgments are © Government of Singapore; reproduction and reuse are governed by the Singapore Courts Terms of Use (https://www.judiciary.gov.sg/terms-of-use). This project is not affiliated with, and is not endorsed by, the Singapore Courts, the Judiciary, or eLitigation. Summaries in the summary column are AI-generated research aids, are not part of the judgment, and may contain errors.
- **Source:** eLitigation — Singapore Courts' free judgments portal (https://www.elitigation.sg/gd/)
- **Source URL:** https://www.elitigation.sg/gd/

### Resources

| Resource | Description | Fragments | Fragments on skip | FTS fields |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `judgments` | One row per judgment. Built in three phases: Phase 1 (discovery) scrapes listing pages for catalog metadata; Phase 2 (enrichment) extracts the full judgment body from the detail page's div#divJudgement into content_text plus per-paragraph rows in judgments_fragments, and captures the court-issued summary from div#divCaseSummary; Phase 3 generates an AI research summary (Facts / Holding / Reasons) with a rolling two-pass LLM pipeline. Backfill is incremental, so during it many rows have content_text IS NULL (not yet extracted) and summary IS NULL (not yet summarised). The HTML source is eLitigation's mobile/web conversion of the judgment — the PDF at pdf_url is the authoritative version. | yes | no | `case_name`, `summary`, `court_summary` |
| `judgments_fragments` | One row per Judg-* element of each extracted judgment — numbered paragraphs, lettered and roman sub-paragraphs, headings, quotes, list items, counsel and hearing-date blocks — in document order. This is the substrate for full-text search (every fragment's content_text is FTS-indexed) and the input the AI summariser reads. Rows are written by the judgments resource's Phase 2 (resources/judgments.py), not by this stub; ids are deterministic and inserts use INSERT OR IGNORE, so re-runs never duplicate rows. Text derives from eLitigation's web-converted HTML; html_raw preserves the source markup verbatim. | no | no | — |

- facets: `['court', 'decision_date', 'has_content']`
- size: `25`
- fragments fts fields: `['content_text']`
- label column: `case_name`
- fragments table: `judgments_fragments`

**`judgments_fragments`**

- facets: `['class_name', 'has_footnotes', 'has_table', 'has_figure']`
- sort: `ordinal`

## Command reference (auto-generated)

```bash
uv run zeeker build                        # build all resources
uv run zeeker build <resource> [...]       # selective build
uv run zeeker build --sync-from-s3         # incremental: download existing DB from S3 first
uv run zeeker build --setup-fts            # (re)create FTS indexes on configured fields (idempotent)
uv run zeeker build --json                 # machine-readable BuildReport JSON on stdout
uv run zeeker build --progress-file p.json # atomic JSON snapshot after each resource (for watchers)
uv run zeeker build --fail-on-blocked      # exit 1 if any resource skipped with kind "blocked"
uv run zeeker deploy                       # upload the built .db to S3
```

## Status contract (auto-generated — zeeker 0.9.0)

This section is baked in verbatim from the installed zeeker version. Monitors
should parse builds against this contract, not against ad-hoc log scraping.

### Exit codes (`zeeker build`)

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | All resources succeeded (skips are not failures). |
| `1` | One or more resources failed, FTS setup failed, post-hook exited non-zero, `--fail-on-empty` with a skipped resource, or `--fail-on-blocked` with a resource that skipped with kind `blocked`. |
| `2` | Fatal error: schema conflict, DB open failure, config error, local-diverged sync. No coherent build ran. |

### Non-TTY line grammar (plain text output, what agents see)

One status line per resource, streamed as each finishes:

```
[OK  ] <resource>  <N> records  (<T>s)
[FAIL] <resource>  <error message>  (<T>s)
[SKIP] <resource>  <reason> (<kind>)  (<T>s)
[SKIP] <resource>  no data returned  (<T>s)
WARN[<resource>]: <message>
WARN[build]: <message>
SUMMARY: <S> succeeded, <F> failed, <K> skipped in <T>s | <k1>=<v1> <k2>=<v2>
FTS_ERROR: <message>
POST_HOOK: <command> exit=<code>
FATAL: <message>
```

- `[SKIP] name  <reason> (kind)` — the resource raised `Skip(reason, kind=...)`;
  the reason says WHY. `[SKIP] name  no data returned` is a plain `return []`
  skip (implicit kind `up_to_date`, no reason).
- Enrichment counters (see below) are appended to `[OK]`/`[SKIP]` lines as
  `; key=value key=value` (never to `[FAIL]` lines), e.g.
  `[SKIP] judgments  no data returned; updated=50 enriched=25  (12.3s)`.
- `WARN[<resource>]:` lines follow that resource's status line; `WARN[build]:`
  lines are build-level warnings (e.g. S3 sync issues).
- The `SUMMARY:` footer aggregates `extra_counts` across all resources after
  a ` | ` separator (omitted when there are no counters).

### Skip kinds and what each means for a monitor

| Kind | Meaning | Bumps `_zeeker_updates.last_updated`? | Monitor action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `up_to_date` | Source was checked; nothing new. The healthy steady state. | Yes | None. |
| `blocked` | A precondition failed (proxy down, missing env var) — the source was NOT checked. | No (time-based incremental resources stay safe) | Actionable: investigate the precondition. Use `--fail-on-blocked` to turn this into exit 1. |
| `disabled` | Intentionally switched off (feature flag / config). | No | None — not an incident. |

### Enrichment counters (`__zeeker_report__`)

Multi-phase resources that UPDATE existing rows (0 records inserted) report
work via a module-level dict in the resource module:

```python
def fetch_data(existing_table):
    global __zeeker_report__
    __zeeker_report__ = {"updated": 50, "enriched": 25, "notes": "phase2 drained 25"}
    return []
```

- Read and cleared on EVERY exit path — success, skip, even a fetch_data crash
  (work done before the crash stays visible).
- Re-read after the fragments phase; counters set in `fetch_fragments_data`
  merge in, summing on key collision.
- Int values only (other value types are ignored, never fail the build).
- Rendered as `key=value` on status lines, aggregated totals in the `SUMMARY:`
  footer, and carried as `extra_counts` / `notes` in `--json`.
- A "0 succeeded" SUMMARY with non-zero counters means real enrichment work
  happened — do not read it as a dead build.

### JSON payload (`--json` and `--progress-file` share the same schema)

Top-level fields:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | string | `success` \| `partial_failure` \| `failed` \| `fatal` |
| `total_duration_s` | float | Whole-build wall time. |
| `resources` | array | One object per resource (fields below). |
| `build_warnings` | array of strings | Build-level warnings (`WARN[build]:` lines). |
| `fts_error` | string or null | FTS setup failure, if any. |
| `fatal_error` | string or null | Set when the build died before/without a per-resource report. |
| `post_hook` | object or null | `{command, exit_code, stdout, stderr}` when `--post-hook` ran. |

Per-resource object fields:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | Resource name. |
| `status` | string | `success` \| `failed` \| `skipped` |
| `records` | int | New main-table rows inserted. |
| `duration_s` | float | Per-resource wall time. |
| `error_message` | string or null | Set on failure. |
| `traceback` | string or null | Full Python traceback on failure (paths CWD-relativized). |
| `fragments_records` | int or null | Fragment rows inserted, when a fragments phase ran. |
| `skip_reason` | string or null | The `Skip(...)` reason; null for plain returned-`[]` skips. |
| `skip_kind` | string or null | `up_to_date` \| `blocked` \| `disabled` (only meaningful when skipped). |
| `warnings` | array of strings | Per-resource warnings (`WARN[<resource>]:` lines). |
| `extra_counts` | object | Int counters from `__zeeker_report__`. |
| `notes` | string or null | Free-text note from `__zeeker_report__`. |

## What happens during a run

Everything happens inside the `judgments` resource. `judgments_fragments`
is a deliberate stub (its `fetch_data` returns `[]`) that exists only to
carry the fragments table's zeeker.toml metadata — it always renders as
`[SKIP] judgments_fragments  no data returned` and that is healthy.

`judgments.fetch_data()` runs **exactly once per build** (zeeker >= 0.9.0
single-fetch lifecycle — no module reload, no second fetch pass) and runs
three phases in order:

1. **Phase 1 — discovery.** Scrapes eLitigation listing pages
   (`?CurrentPage=N`, 10 judgments/page, sorted date-desc) for catalog
   metadata. During the initial archive crawl it walks up to
   `JUDGMENTS_MAX_PAGES_PER_RUN` pages per build, resuming from
   `checkpoint_judgments_discovery.json`. In steady state it stops after
   `JUDGMENTS_INCREMENTAL_STOP` consecutive already-known IDs — but only
   after fully scanning the first `JUDGMENTS_MIN_PAGES_PER_RUN` pages
   (coverage floor: late-published judgments slot into the listing at
   their decision-date position, below newer arrivals, so early pages
   can hold long runs of known IDs while deeper pages still hold unseen
   rows). In steady state the walk typically ends within the guaranteed
   pages and clears the checkpoint. New rows are returned to
   zeeker for insert; content columns start NULL.
2. **Phase 2 — enrichment.** Reuses the same `httpx.Client`. Picks up to
   `JUDGMENTS_EXTRACT_MAX_PER_RUN` rows with `content_text IS NULL`
   (newest decision_date first), fetches each detail page, parses
   paragraphs/tables/footnotes, UPDATEs the main row, and inserts
   per-paragraph rows into `judgments_fragments` in the same transaction
   (NOT via the fragments pipeline). Raw HTML and parsed output are
   cached under `.cache/`. Skipped entirely if Phase 1's circuit breaker
   tripped.
3. **Phase 3 — AI summaries.** Uses its own OpenAI-compatible client
   (`LLM_BASE_URL`; skips gracefully when unset). Picks up to
   `JUDGMENTS_SUMMARY_MAX_PER_RUN` rows with
   `has_content = 1 AND summary IS NULL`, rolling-summarises the
   fragments, and UPDATEs `summary`/`summary_generated_at`. Docs that
   repeatedly fail on the primary model escalate to the alt endpoint
   (`LLM_BASE_URL_2`), then hard-quarantine. Progress is appended to
   `phase3_progress.jsonl` for live monitoring.

**Status-line semantics after 0.9.0 adoption:**

- Phases 2+3 report their work via `__zeeker_report__` counters:
  `extracted`, `summarised`, `extract_backlog`, `summary_backlog`, plus a
  `notes` string. They appear on the `[OK]`/`[SKIP]` line and in `--json`
  (`extra_counts`/`notes`).
- Steady-state healthy build:
  `[SKIP] judgments  no data returned; extracted=50 summarised=50 extract_backlog=NNNN summary_backlog=NN` —
  zero new rows discovered but real enrichment work happened. Do NOT read
  this as a dead build.
- When discovery **aborts** (fetch failure / HTTP error / circuit
  breaker) and no rows were staged AND Phases 2+3 did no work either, the
  resource raises `Skip("discovery aborted: <reason>", kind="blocked")` —
  the freshness marker does not advance and the skip is actionable. If
  any partial work happened (rows staged, docs extracted or summarised)
  it returns normally so the progress is persisted.
- Typical healthy log inside the resource: `Existing records in
  database: N` → `Fetching page 1 …` → `Stopping: 5 consecutive known
  IDs — steady-state mode.` → `Discovery OK: 0 new records, …` →
  `Phase 2: enriching up to 50 / NNNN remaining …` → `Phase 2 complete:
  …` → `Phase 3: summarising up to 50 / NN remaining …` → `Phase 3
  complete: …`.

## Environment variables

Phases 1 and 2 need **no env vars for correctness** (public-HTML crawl).
Phase 3 needs `LLM_BASE_URL` to do anything; without it Phase 3 logs
"LLM not configured — skipping" and the build still succeeds. Values live
in the project `.env` (auto-loaded by zeeker; see `.env.example`) — there
are no CI secrets because deployment is not wired up yet.

| Env var | Default | What it controls |
|---|---|---|
| `JUDGMENTS_MAX_PAGES_PER_RUN` | `50` | Phase 1: batch cap on listing pages per invocation. Set to `2` for smoke tests. |
| `JUDGMENTS_MIN_PAGES_PER_RUN` | `10` | Phase 1: coverage floor — always fully scan the first N listing pages before the steady-state known-ID early exit is honoured (from page N+1 onward). Late-published judgments slot into the date-sorted listing at their decision-date position, so early pages can hold long runs of known IDs while deeper pages still hold unseen rows. `0` restores the original first-trip stop. Clamped to `JUDGMENTS_MAX_PAGES_PER_RUN` when larger. |
| `JUDGMENTS_INCREMENTAL_STOP` | `5` | Phase 1: consecutive already-known IDs before early exit (suppressed within the `JUDGMENTS_MIN_PAGES_PER_RUN` floor). |
| `JUDGMENTS_DELAY_BASE` / `JUDGMENTS_DELAY_JITTER` | `1.5` / `0.5` | Phase 1: polite sleep (s) between listing fetches, +/- jitter. |
| `JUDGMENTS_EXTRACT_ENABLED` | `1` | Phase 2: `0` = discovery only (skip enrichment). |
| `JUDGMENTS_EXTRACT_MAX_PER_RUN` | `50` | Phase 2: max docs enriched per build. |
| `JUDGMENTS_EXTRACT_MAX_RETRIES` | `3` | Phase 2: failures before a doc is quarantined. |
| `JUDGMENTS_EXTRACT_RETRY_AFTER` | `86400` | Phase 2: quarantine TTL in seconds (24h). |
| `JUDGMENTS_EXTRACT_DELAY_BASE` / `JUDGMENTS_EXTRACT_DELAY_JITTER` | `1.5` / `0.5` | Phase 2: sleep between detail-page fetches. |
| `JUDGMENTS_SUMMARY_ENABLED` | `1` | Phase 3: `0` = skip summarisation. |
| `JUDGMENTS_SUMMARY_MAX_PER_RUN` | `50` | Phase 3: max docs summarised per build. |
| `JUDGMENTS_SUMMARY_MAX_BATCHES` | `20` | Phase 3: rolling-pass batch cap per doc (primary model). |
| `JUDGMENTS_SUMMARY_MAX_RETRIES` | `3` | Phase 3: primary-model failures before a doc escalates to the alt-model priority pool. |
| `JUDGMENTS_SUMMARY_HARD_FAIL_LIMIT` | `6` | Phase 3: TOTAL failures (primary + alt) before hard quarantine. |
| `JUDGMENTS_SUMMARY_RETRY_AFTER_HARD` | `604800` | Phase 3: hard-quarantine TTL in seconds (1 week). |
| `JUDGMENTS_SUMMARY_MAX_INPUT_CHARS` | `32000` | Phase 3: char budget for composed LLM input (~8K tokens). |
| `LLM_BASE_URL` | *unset* | Phase 3: OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Unset → Phase 3 skips. |
| `LLM_API_KEY` | `not-needed` | Phase 3: optional for local servers (Ollama/vLLM); required for cloud. |
| `LLM_MODEL` | `llama3.1:8b` | Phase 3: primary model name. |
| `LLM_BASE_URL_2` / `LLM_API_KEY_2` / `LLM_MODEL_2` | *unset* / falls back / same as primary | Phase 3: alt endpoint for docs at ≥3 primary failures. Unset → no escalation, quarantine behaviour unchanged. |
| `JUDGMENTS_SUMMARY_MAX_BATCHES_ALT` | `5` | Phase 3: rolling-pass cap for alt-model calls (fewer, wider batches). |
| `JUDGMENTS_SUMMARY_MAX_TOKENS_ALT` | `8192` | Phase 3: output-token floor for alt-model calls. |
| `JUDGMENTS_SUMMARY_TEMPERATURE` / `TOP_P` / `FREQUENCY_PENALTY` / `PRESENCE_PENALTY` / `SEED` | `0.0` / `0.9` / `0.15` / `0.1` / `42` | Phase 3: sampling knobs (deterministic extraction defaults). |
| `JUDGMENTS_SUMMARY_REPEAT_PENALTY` / `JUDGMENTS_SUMMARY_TOP_K` | `1.2` / `20` | Phase 3: Ollama-specific knobs (via `extra_body`). |
| `S3_BUCKET`, `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `S3_ENDPOINT_URL` | *unset* | `zeeker deploy` only — deployment is currently deferred. |

## Cadence & expected yield

- **Schedule:** every 6 hours at :07 UTC (`7 */6 * * *` in the system
  crontab, via `~/.local/bin/zeeker-build zeeker-judgements`; log at
  `~/logs/cron/zeeker-judgements.log`).
- **New judgments (Phase 1):** 0–5 per day — typically 1–3 on court
  sitting days, 0 on weekends/holidays. `records` on the `[OK]` line, or
  `[SKIP] … no data returned` with counters in steady state.
- **Phase 2 enrichment:** up to `JUDGMENTS_EXTRACT_MAX_PER_RUN` (50)
  rows per run; `extracted=` counter shows the actual number and
  `extract_backlog=` the remaining NULL-content rows (~8,700 as of Jul
  2026 → months of runs to drain at current caps).
- **Phase 3 summarisation:** up to `JUDGMENTS_SUMMARY_MAX_PER_RUN` (50)
  rows per run; `summarised=` / `summary_backlog=` counters. Backlog is
  bounded by Phase 2 progress (only enriched rows are summarisable).
- **Duration:** 30–45 minutes is normal, dominated by Phase 3 LLM calls
  (and Phase 2 polite delays), not discovery. Steady-state discovery
  alone is seconds.
- **Anomalies worth flagging:** build > 2h; `extracted=0` with a large
  `extract_backlog` and no quarantine explanation; `summarised=0` for
  multiple days while `summary_backlog > 0`; any `[SKIP] … (blocked)`;
  `extract_backlog`/`summary_backlog` not shrinking across a week.

## Failure modes & recovery

**Retry / circuit-breaker behaviour (Phases 1–2):** every HTTP fetch gets
3 tenacity attempts with exponential backoff; 5 consecutive failures trip
a circuit breaker (60s cooldown, then abort with checkpoint saved). If
Phase 1 trips the breaker, Phase 2 is skipped for that run.

**Failure modes:**

1. **eLitigation unreachable / erroring.** Discovery aborts. If nothing
   else got done either, the build shows
   `[SKIP] judgments  discovery aborted: <reason> (blocked)` — the
   freshness marker does NOT advance. Transient; next run resumes from
   `checkpoint_judgments_discovery.json`. Persistent `blocked` skips
   (2+ days) mean the site changed or is blocking the bot — investigate.
2. **A single broken detail page (Phase 2).** After
   `JUDGMENTS_EXTRACT_MAX_RETRIES` (3) failures the doc is quarantined
   for `JUDGMENTS_EXTRACT_RETRY_AFTER` (24h) in
   `checkpoint_judgments_extraction.json`, so it can't burn the whole
   budget. Structurally empty pages are marked `has_content=0` once and
   never retried.
3. **LLM endpoint down (Phase 3).** `llm failed: …` per doc; failures
   are tracked in `checkpoint_judgments_summary.json`. Escalation
   ladder: <3 failures → retried on the primary model each build; 3–5 →
   priority pool, retried first on the alt endpoint (`LLM_BASE_URL_2`,
   when set), bypassing any TTL; ≥`JUDGMENTS_SUMMARY_HARD_FAIL_LIMIT`
   (6) total → hard-quarantined, one attempt per
   `JUDGMENTS_SUMMARY_RETRY_AFTER_HARD` (1 week).
4. **Crash mid-run.** Safe. All checkpoint/cache writes are atomic
   (tmp + `os.replace`); fragment inserts are `INSERT OR IGNORE` on
   deterministic PKs; the next run recovers cached-but-unwritten work
   from disk without re-fetching or re-calling the LLM.

**State files (all gitignored, all safe to inspect):**

- `checkpoint_judgments_discovery.json` — Phase 1 resume state. Delete to
  force discovery to restart from page 1 (steady-state runs clear it
  themselves).
- `checkpoint_judgments_extraction.json` / `checkpoint_judgments_summary.json`
  — per-doc failure counts + quarantine timestamps only (NOT progress).
  Delete an entry (or the file) to force immediate retries.
- `phase3_progress.jsonl` — append-only Phase 3 event log for monitors.

**Caches under `.cache/` (two-layer, gitignored):**

- `.cache/judgments_html/{id}.html.gz` — raw detail-page HTML. Deleting
  forces re-fetch from the server (DB state unaffected).
- `.cache/judgments_extractions/{id}.json` — parsed extraction output.
  If parsing rules change: delete these, keep the HTML archive, reset the
  affected rows' `content_text` to NULL, re-run — re-parses from disk
  with **no server traffic**.
- `.cache/judgments_summaries/{id}.json` — LLM output awaiting/duplicating
  the DB write. If prompting rules change: delete these and reset the
  rows' `summary` to NULL to force regeneration. Corrupt JSON is
  auto-quarantined (renamed aside).

## Backlog / progress queries

The `extract_backlog` / `summary_backlog` counters on every build line are
computed from exactly these queries — use the SQL to verify independently
(`sqlite3 zeeker-judgements.db "<query>"`):

```sql
-- Phase 2 backlog: rows not yet enriched
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM judgments WHERE content_text IS NULL;

-- Phase 3 backlog: enriched rows not yet summarised
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM judgments WHERE has_content = 1 AND summary IS NULL;

-- Overall pipeline state at a glance
SELECT COUNT(*) AS total,
       SUM(content_text IS NOT NULL) AS enriched,
       SUM(has_content = 1) AS with_body,
       SUM(summary IS NOT NULL) AS summarised
FROM judgments;

-- Fragment volume (grows with each Phase 2 run)
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM judgments_fragments;

-- What did the last builds actually write?
SELECT * FROM _zeeker_updates;

-- Recent Phase 2 output (spot-check freshness)
SELECT citation, extracted_at FROM judgments
WHERE extracted_at IS NOT NULL ORDER BY extracted_at DESC LIMIT 10;

-- Recent Phase 3 output
SELECT citation, summary_generated_at FROM judgments
WHERE summary_generated_at IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY summary_generated_at DESC LIMIT 10;
```

A build "advanced the pipeline" iff at least one of: `records > 0`,
`extracted > 0`, or `summarised > 0` — equivalently, one of the two
backlog counters went down (or new rows pushed `extract_backlog` up while
`extracted` still ran). The failure-checkpoint JSON files are NOT progress
signals; they only track what was tried and failed.

## Escalation

There is no paging infrastructure for this project — builds are run and
watched by the owner's monitoring agent. Sensible thresholds:

- **Notify the owner** when: `[SKIP] … (blocked)` on 2+ consecutive daily
  runs (source outage or bot-blocking); any `[FAIL]`/`FATAL` that recurs
  on re-run; `summarised=0` with `summary_backlog > 0` for 3+ days (LLM
  endpoint misconfigured/down); a schema-conflict exit (code 2).
- **Do not escalate**: single blocked skips (transient outages),
  `judgments_fragments` skips (always), steady-state
  `no data returned` lines with healthy counters, or hard-quarantined
  stragglers in the checkpoint files.
- Live Phase 3 visibility: `tail -f phase3_progress.jsonl` during a run;
  `zeeker build --progress-file p.json` for a machine-readable snapshot
  after each resource.
